full_judgment: 10. The modified record-of-right, as in evident from the provision of sec. 46 of the Act, was required to be prepared and considered for the purpose of final publication of the compensation assessment roll regarding acquisition of all kind of rent receiving interest under the Act. The record of right derives its presumptive value of correctness both under section 19 of the Act as well as section 144 of the Act. In the absence of any final publication of the record of right which have been prepared under the Act either under section 19 or under section 144, there cannot be any presumptive value of its correctness which is required to be rebutted. It does not a from the judgments of the Courts below that they considered as to whether this sub-division of the original jama was done upon the application of the pre-emptor or with notice to him as provided under section 117 (1) (c) of the Act. Preparation of the record-of-right under Chapter IV was for the purpose of acquisition of rent receiving interest whereas the purpose of preparation of the record-of right under Part-V, Chapter-XIV is for maintaining the proper and up-to-date settlement rent roll. It should be significantly noted that whenever the raiyat or under raiyat or any other raiyat as they had been under the Bengal Tenancy Act, alter coming into force of Part-V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 have been merged into a single status of malik having their equal rights and liabilities including the right to pre-empt any land under section 96 of the Act. Thus in the absence of any material or evidence on record that such separation of original jama was done in accordance with section 117(1) (c) of is not at all safe to oust a co-sharer malik from exercising his vested right only on the basis of two M.R.O R. Khatians which were prepared initially for the purpose of realisation of rent pending final publication of record-of-right as has been contemplated under the scheme of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
